title: FHFA House Price Index — Monthly Index (November 2026 data), 9:00 a.m. ET
source: FHFA: two FHFA primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06, independently of the sweep that proposed this id. (1) fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes) — its "2027 HPI Release Dates" table reads "Tuesday, January 26 | Monthly Index | November 2026", the first of twelve dated 2027 rows (Jan 26 -> Dec 28, every one a last Tuesday). (2) The published 2026Q2 report (HTTP 200, 1,522,949 bytes, released 2026-08-25), whose "FHFA HPI Release Dates for 2027" appendix page carries the identical row and states above it: "Public FHFA HPI(R) releases occur at 9AM ET and include a press release, tables, figures, and associated data" — a published document, not a second reading of the same web table. Promoted estimate -> confirmed on the precedent construction-spending-2026-12-01, new-home-sales-2026-11-25, fhfa-hpi-2026-11-24 and fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29 set: the no-self-confirm limit binds the DISCOVERING sweep (fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29), not this event's own independent second look. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29 initial-research sweep (2026-09-06) and researched the same day; the proposal file is now shadowed by this canonical one. INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-06 (docs/research/events/fhfa-hpi-2027-01-26.md) found the distinguishing feature is NOT the funding fork the proposal named but a mechanical calendar collision neither sibling saw: FOMC meetings run Tuesday-Wednesday and FHFA publishes on the last Tuesday, so an FHFA release can NEVER fall on an FOMC decision day (always a Wednesday) and falls on FOMC DAY ONE whenever the meeting opens on a last Tuesday. Measured: 17 of the 68 FHFA release days since 2021 are FOMC day 1, ZERO are decision days — and in January the collision is systematic, 8 of 8 across 2021-2028 using the Fed's own posted dates (2021-01-26, 2022-01-25, 2023-01-31, 2024-01-30, 2025-01-28, 2026-01-27, 2027-01-26, and the Board's posted 2028-01-25). This print therefore lands inside fomc-blackout-start-2027-01-16 (through 01-28), on day one of the FOMC's ANNUAL ORGANIZATIONAL meeting, with fomc-2027-01-27 the next morning. The tape consequence inverts the sibling's year-end finding on the SAME statistic: FOMC day-1 sessions carry VIX9D/VIX at a median 0.9996 vs a 0.9260 baseline (n=45, p=0.0000) -- the front of the curve is bid to FLAT because the nine-day window spans the decision -- where fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29's Dec 24-31 window measured 0.9060 vs 0.9421 (p=0.0076), compressed. Any lane copying December's 'quiet thin-tape ceiling' forward would be wrong: the six January FHFA sessions since 2021 printed SPX |c2c| of 0.149 / 1.217 / 1.464 / 0.060 / 0.922 / 0.408%, two of them ABOVE the 1.1028% release-day p75, against December's five all at or under 0.428%. IMPACT STAYS low deliberately -- the session is loud because of the FOMC, not because of this print, and raising the tier would mis-attribute the FOMC's impact to FHFA. Also corrected here from the full archive (271 rows, 11 pages, re-parsed today): the sibling's 'December is the one month FHFA has historically moved' does not survive the per-month control -- December is 6/18 but July is 7/19, January 8/17, March and April 9/19; pre-2021 the last-Tuesday match rate is 50 of 154 (32.5%) across ALL months and 68 of 68 (100%) since. The last-Tuesday rule is a post-2020 policy, not a December quirk. symbols: [] and 0 hits for any house-price keying in trade-playbooks.md or multi-symbol-sweep.md (re-grepped 2026-09-06); nothing here licenses an entry.
